title: Perimeter, area and volume
ks3: Geometry and measures: perimeter, area, circles, volume and surface area
intro: How far round, how much surface, how much space inside. Practise perimeter and area of rectangles, triangles and compound shapes, circles, and the volume of cuboids.
description: Free KS3 Maths perimeter, area and volume questions with answers: rectangles, triangles, parallelograms, trapeziums, compound shapes, circles, cuboids and surface area. Marked instantly, for Year 7, 8 and 9 (ages 9 to 14).

questions.q: What is the perimeter of the rectangle?
questions.hint: Perimeter is the distance all the way round. Add all four sides.

questions.q: What is the area of the rectangle?
questions.hint: Area of a rectangle = length × width.
questions.explain: 8 × 5 = 40 cm². Area is measured in square units.

questions.q: A square has a perimeter of 36 cm. What is its area?
questions.hint: Find the length of one side first.
questions.explain: A square has 4 equal sides, so each side is 36 ÷ 4 = 9 cm. Area = 9 × 9 = 81 cm².

questions.q: A garden lawn is 12 m long and 7 m wide. Turf costs £5 per square metre. How much does it cost to turf the whole lawn, in pounds?
What is the area of the triangle?
questions.hint: Area of a triangle = base × height ÷ 2.
questions.explain: 6 × 4 = 24, and 24 ÷ 2 = 12 cm². A triangle is half of a rectangle.

questions.q: A parallelogram has a base of 9 cm and a perpendicular height of 4 cm. What is its area?
questions.hint: Area of a parallelogram = base × perpendicular height.
questions.explain: 9 × 4 = 36 cm². (Cut off a triangle from one end and move it to the other: it becomes a rectangle.)

questions.q: A trapezium has parallel sides of 5 cm and 9 cm, and a height of 4 cm. What is its area?
questions.hint: Area = (a + b) ÷ 2 × height, where a and b are the parallel sides.

questions.q: What is the area of the L shape?
questions.hint: Work out the big rectangle, then take away the missing corner.
questions.explain: Big rectangle: 10 × 8 = 80 cm². Missing corner: 4 × 3 = 12 cm². Area = 80 − 12 = 68 cm².

questions.q: What is the perimeter of the L shape?
questions.hint: Work out the two missing side lengths first: 10 − 6 and 8 − 5.
questions.explain: The missing sides are 4 cm and 3 cm. Perimeter = 10 + 8 + 6 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 36 cm. (It is the same as the perimeter of the 10 × 8 rectangle.)

questions.q: A circle has a diameter of 10 cm. Use π = 3.14 to find its circumference.
A circle has a radius of 5 cm. Use π = 3.14 to find its area.
questions.hint: Area of a circle = π × radius × radius.

questions.q: What is the volume of the cuboid?
How many 1 cm cubes fit inside a cube with 4 cm sides?
questions.hint: Volume of a cube = side × side × side.

questions.q: What is the total surface area of the cuboid?
questions.hint: A cuboid has 6 faces in 3 matching pairs.
questions.explain: The faces are 5 × 3 = 15, 5 × 2 = 10 and 3 × 2 = 6, two of each. 2 × (15 + 10 + 6) = 62 cm².

questions.q: Which unit would you use for the area of a football pitch?
questions.explain: Area is measured in square units, and a football pitch is measured in metres, so m². (m³ is for volume.)

questions.q: How many square centimetres are there in 1 square metre?
questions.hint: A 1 m by 1 m square is 100 cm by 100 cm.

questions.q: A fish tank is 50 cm long, 30 cm wide and 40 cm tall. How many litres of water does it hold when full? (1 litre = 1000 cm³)
questions.hint: Find the volume in cm³, then divide by 1000.
